title: EOMasters Newsletter #015
description: A hand-picked selection of news from the field of EO and RS
html:
EOMasters Newsletter #015

14/01/2024

Happy New Year everyone!

It is already the middle of January and I hope your year has started well and if not, rest assured that it will get better. I'm looking forward to finally releasing my first software to you. I am just waiting for the release of SNAP 10.

Let's see what news we have in this new year 2024.

EO and RS News

CryoSat Data Products Delayed

The delivery of CryoSat data products is currently delayed. This is due to a technical issue at the Payload Data Ground Segment (PDGS). The issue is currently under investigation.

  • Delay in the availability for CryoSat Products - Earth Online (esa.int)

GEOSAT collaborates with ESA to boost understanding of the planet

GEOSAT datasets are currently being disseminated via the TPM programme and more data are expected to be made available in the coming months. GEOSAT-2 provides resolutions of up to 40 cm by using artificial intelligence.

  • GEOSAT collaborates with ESA to boost understanding of the planet - Earth Online

  • New Super Resolution product for GEOSAT-2 - Earth Online (esa.int)

Copernicus Thematic Hubs in the Limelight

In November 2023 the Copernicus Thematic Hubs were launched. A series of articles will show case the Copernicus hubs in closer detail. In the first article an overview of the health, coastal, energy and arctic hubs is provided.

  • OBSERVER: An Exploration of the Copernicus Thematic Hubs | Copernicus

Recent Landsat 8 Acquisitions Need to be Reprocessed

Some Landsat 8 products created from data collected between January 1st and January 6th, 2024, must be corrected due to a problem with radiometric values that were changed in a recent Landsat 8 CPF file. The wrong gain adjustment affected the coastal aerosol Band 1 by about 0.3 percent and the blue Band 2 by about 0.1 percent.

In total, 4,272 Landsat 8 Level-1 products are affected and need to be fixed.

  • Reprocessing of Landsat 8 Data Acquired January 1-6, 2024 | U.S. Geological Survey (usgs.gov)

Virtual Event – How Satellites Monitor Atmospheric Methane

You can now register for a virtual event about monitoring atmospheric methane by satellites. The importance of these observations and campaigns to monitor methane are discussed.

It'll take place on January 22nd at 19:00 CET (01:00 pm ET)

  • Virtual Event - Not Invisible Anymore: How satellites monitor atmospheric methane - SpaceNews

Software, Tools and Services

Esri ArcGis News

Esri highlights the new features of the ArcGIS GeoAnalytics Engine v1.3. These are besides other feature enhancements Geocoding and Network Analysis. The geocoding allows to turn geo-coordinates into addresses and reverse. The network analysis tools allow using network datasets (roads, railways, utilities, etc.) to answer questions about connectivity and proximity.

  • What’s New in ArcGIS GeoAnalytics Engine 1.3 (esri.com)

Beyond EO

Why Keeping a Streak Boosts Your Motivation

This is an article of personal interest. I'm currently on a rowing kick. I have had a water rowing machine at home for a few years. I used it from time to time. But I was disappointed that I didn't use it regularly. They say you need 90 days to get into the habit. So I started my current rowing streak.

Today my streak is 40 days long and every day I write it down in a chart. I can say that it is really motivating. Seeing the streak grow gives me a boost and I don't want to break it. Writing down my rowing performance and seeing how it increases is also very motivating.

  • Why Keeping a Streak Boosts Your Motivation

Newsletter Archive

For past editions of this newsletter, you can visit the archive.

That's it for this issue. I hope you enjoyed this collection of news. Stay tuned for the next edition, which will arrive in your inbox in about two weeks.

Tschüss and Goodbye!

Marco
